control.detail: Nothing a player or an NPC does adds a person for their own sake. A person is minted when a named role or a screen needs one — election turnover, or a scene short of somebody — and never otherwise. There is no in-migration, which is also why nothing assigns anyone a party.

playerReachDetail: A player can see a population number and can never meet the people it counts, or affect how many there are.

surface.detail: A place's population is shown, but it is the sourced headcount, not a count of anybody the game simulates. Nothing on any screen reports that the world's population has changed, or that the people in it are not what the number counts.

system.detail: Two populations, and they never touch. A few hundred simulated people are the entire cast, and a real sourced headcount is carried for each place. The simulated people are not declared a sample of the sourced one, carry no weight, and nothing scales anything by the ratio between them. Economic readings come off the real series; social and political life comes off the few hundred records. An election is computed from neither: the result is a campaign support score plus a random swing, spread so the shares total a hundred, with no electorate anywhere in the game.

title: Who lives in the world, and who the numbers are about
